name: Howard Fast
bio: Howard Fast was a novelist (author of Citizen Tom Paine and, later, Spartacus) and a Communist Party member who served as a trustee of the Joint Anti-Fascist Refugee Committee, which aided refugees from Franco's Spain. Cited for contempt of Congress after refusing to surrender the committee's records and donor names to the House Un-American Activities Committee, he served a three-month federal prison term in 1950 — conceiving the novel Spartacus while jailed. The biography Two Who Were There notes that by 1950 Fast, among the era's 'most outstanding fighters for peace,' was 'already in prison.'
charges: Contempt of Congress — refusing to turn over Joint Anti-Fascist Refugee Committee records and donor names to HUAC
convicted: Convicted of contempt of Congress; imprisoned 1950

name: George Pirinsky
bio: George Pirinsky was the executive secretary of the American Slav Congress, a Popular Front coalition of Slavic-American organizations, and secretary of the Macedonian-American People's League. During the McCarthy-era crackdown he was arrested for deportation; his bond was canceled and he was imprisoned on Ellis Island — held ninety-one days in solitary confinement before any deportation order was issued. As recorded in the biography Two Who Were There, he called his arrest 'a deliberate attempt to intimidate Slavic Americans.' In September 1951 he became the first person deported under the McCarran Act, sailing from the United States aboard a Danish freighter bound, by way of Copenhagen, for his native Bulgaria.
charges: McCarran / Walter-McCarran Act deportation — leadership of the American Slav Congress
sentence: 91 days in solitary on Ellis Island; first person deported under the McCarran Act — exiled to Bulgaria

name: Henry Podolski
bio: Henry Podolski was a Polish-language editor of Glos Ludowy, the Detroit-based Polish Daily People's Voice, a left-wing labor newspaper. During the McCarthy-era deportation drive he was arrested and held in jail after deportation proceedings were instituted against him beginning in 1949. He and his U.S.-born wife, Dolores, were ultimately forced to leave for Poland, settling there as permanent residents — among the former Detroiters the biography Two Who Were There describes as 'victims of the McCarthy era and deportees under the Walter-McCarran Law.' In Poland he worked in Polish radio.
charges: Walter-McCarran Act deportation — editing a left-wing Polish-American newspaper
convicted: Arrested 1949; deportation proceedings; deported to Poland (c. 1951)
sentence: Jailed pending deportation; exiled to Poland

name: James Papandreau
bio: James (Jimmy) Papandreau was a Greek-American activist in progressive and Democratic circles in Detroit. During the McCarthy-era deportation crackdown he was arrested on deportation charges similar to those brought against the Glos Ludowy editor Henry Podolski, and was later deported. The biography Two Who Were There lists him among the former Detroiters living in Warsaw — 'victims of the McCarthy era and deportees under the Walter-McCarran Law.'
charges: Walter-McCarran Act deportation — Detroit progressive/left-wing activism
sentence: Arrested for deportation; exiled to Poland
